lines.narration: When doctors stitch you shut, some thread is never coming out.
Nobody removes it. Nobody pulls anything.
The thread is engineered to vanish inside you.
It's a polymer chain: thousands of links, sewn into your skin.
Each water molecule slips in and snaps one link.
Week one, the thread still holds your wound shut.
By week two, it's lost half its strength.
Your cleanup cells swallow the fragments whole.
Inside your body, there is no other exit.
So the thread is tuned: fast for skin, slow for muscle.
Some stitches outlive you — the permanent kind never dissolves.
The best stitches are the ones your body erases.
